1 طَنِخَ , (S, L, K,) aor.
طَنَخَ , (K,) inf. n. طَنَخٌ, (S,) His (a man's, S) heart (قَلْب [meaning stomach, which is often thus termed in the present day,]) became overpowered by grease [or greasy food], and he suffered indigestion, (S, L, K,) in consequence thereof; (S, L;) as also تَنِخَ, aor.
طَنَخَ , inf. n. تَنَخٌ. (L.) And طَنِخَتْ said of camels, They suffered indigestion. (TA in art. طنح.) And طَنِخَتْ نَفْسُهُ His soul [or stomach] became heavy; or heaved, or became agitated by a tendency to vomit. (L.) ―
-b2- And He became fat. (L, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
